As the theater director, pick as few stagehands as possible so that every set piece adjacency is handled by a stagehand positioned at a connected piece.
As the clinic manager, staff as small a set of nurses as needed so that every patient pairing has a nurse assigned to at least one of the pair.
As the landlord, install as few door locks as you can so that every shared hallway connection has a lock on an adjoining apartment door.
As the logistics coordinator, allocate as few inspection points as possible so that every route segment is inspected from a checkpoint at a linked hub.
As the school counselor, select as few mentors as practical so that every friendship link among students has a mentor attached to either student.
As the museum exhibit designer, mount as few information panels as necessary so that every exhibit adjacency has a panel at an adjacent display.
As the community organizer, designate as few neighborhood liaisons as needed so that every bordering property pair has a liaison representing at least one side.
As the emergency planner, place as few first aid stations as feasible so that every venue connection is covered by a station located at a connected area.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One end room (room identifier) of a specific corridor. Paired with 'v' to describe a corridor; since corridors are undirected the order is not significant.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of houses along the block that could host a volunteer — i.e., the number of vertices in the neighborhood graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring house pairs along the block that must be covered (each pair of adjacent houses corresponds to one edge in the graph).

item_fields.name: u

item_fields.name: v

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct shelving zones (sections of stacks) in the library layout. This corresponds to the number of vertices in the graph and tells you how many zones are available to staff; zone identifiers referenced elsewhere range over these zones.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring borders between shelving zones. Each border corresponds to an edge in the graph and must be adjacent to at least one staffed zone for the plan to be valid; this number counts how many such borders must be covered.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one endpoint of a shared border — i.e., one of the two neighboring shelving zones that meet at this border. Paired with 'v', it defines a specific border that must be next to a staffed zone.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other endpoint of a shared border — the second shelving zone adjacent to this border. Together with 'u' it specifies a border; the staffing plan must staff at least one of these two zones to cover that border.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of routers in the rack (the number of vertices). Use this as the count of distinct devices you can choose to mark for monitoring.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of direct physical cables between routers (the number of edges). Every one of these cables must have at least one endpoint router marked.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint router for a specific cable (a vertex ID). Paired with 'v' it defines a cable that must be covered by marking at least one endpoint.

item_fields.name: v

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairs of neighboring workstations (adjacent station pairs). Each pair represents two stations that share a border or adjacency and therefore requires at least one of those two stations to have a cook.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one workstation in an adjacent pair. Along with 'v', this names a specific neighboring pair of stations (an adjacency) that must be covered by at least one cook at either endpoint.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other workstation in an adjacent pair. Together with 'u' it specifies a neighboring pair of stations whose adjacency must have at least one cook assigned.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of classrooms in the school layout (each classroom corresponds to a graph vertex). Use this to know how many rooms are available to place supervising teachers.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of hallways that connect pairs of classrooms (each hallway corresponds to an undirected edge). Every hallway must have at least one of its endpoint classrooms staffed.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of one classroom at one end of a specific hallway. When selecting staffed rooms, ensure this classroom covers its incident hallways.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the other classroom at the other end of the same hallway. Each hallway is specified by a pair of such classroom endpoints.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of vendor booths in the expo (the number of vertices). Booths are identified by integers in the instance; use this to validate booth identifiers and to size the checkpoint selection.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of aisles running between pairs of booths (the number of edges). Each aisle must be covered by placing a checkpoint at one of its endpoint booths.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one endpoint booth for a specific aisle. Putting a checkpoint at this booth covers the aisle that links this booth to the paired booth (v). Identifier must refer to an existing booth (1..total_booths).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other endpoint booth for the same aisle. A checkpoint at this booth also covers the aisle. Together with 'aisle_booth_u', this defines an aisle that must have at least one endpoint selected for a checkpoint.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers (machines) in the office network; each server is a vertex in the graph and is identified by an integer or label.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of physical links (network cables) between pairs of servers; each link is an undirected edge that must be covered by at least one updated server.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a specific network link: the identifier (index or label) of the first server connected by this cable. The link is undirected, so this is one of the two servers that must have at least one updated endpoint.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same network link: the identifier (index or label) of the second server connected by this cable. Together with connected_server_1 this defines a cable that must be covered by an update on at least one end.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of trailheads in the park (the vertices). This is the count of candidate locations where a trash bin can be installed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of trail segments (undirected connections between trailheads). Each segment must have at least one of its endpoint trailheads equipped with a bin.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one endpoint trailhead of a specific trail segment. Together with 'v' it names the two trailheads joined by that segment; the solver must ensure at least one of them gets a bin.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other endpoint trailhead of the trail segment paired with 'u'. At least one of 'trailhead_one' or 'trailhead_two' must be selected to install a bin to cover this segment.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students in the group (i.e., the number of vertices in the collaboration graph). Use this to know how many possible mentor candidates exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of student collaboration ties that must be covered (i.e., the number of undirected edges). Each such pair requires at least one of its two students to be chosen as a mentor.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the first student in a collaboration pair. This is one endpoint of an undirected tie; selecting this student as a mentor covers that collaboration.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the second student in the collaboration pair. Together with 'student_a_id', it defines a collaboration that must be covered by choosing at least one of the two students as a mentor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rooms in the plant (the vertices). This counts all distinct room identifiers among which technicians can be stationed; the goal is to minimize how many of these rooms are staffed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pipes that run between pairs of rooms (the edges). Every pipe must have at least one of its endpoint rooms assigned a technician to be considered covered.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (number or label) of one room at one end of a pipe. Assigning a technician to this room will cover all pipes incident to it, including this pipe. Order is not significant because pipes are undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (number or label) of the other room at the opposite end of the pipe. Together with 'room_a' this pair denotes a pipe; staffing either room covers that pipe.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of authors in the coauthorship network — each author is a vertex and represents a potential advisor the editor could invite.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of coauthorship links between authors — each link (edge) must be overseen by inviting at least one of its endpoint authors.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a coauthorship link: the identifier (e.g., index or label) of the first author in this author pair. Inviting this author would cover this specific coauthorship link.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the coauthorship link: the identifier of the second author in this author pair. At least one of author_one or author_two must be invited to cover this link.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of products / display stands in the shop (the number of vertices in the graph). Each product is identified by an integer from 1 to this number; these are the stands you may choose to stock.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of pairs of products that share a shelf (the number of edges). Each such pair requires that at least one of the two product stands in the pair be stocked to cover that shared-shelf relationship.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (vertex number) of the first product in a shared-shelf pair. Together with 'product_v' this defines two products that share a shelf; stocking at least one of these is required to cover that pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (vertex number) of the second product in a shared-shelf pair. Paired with 'product_u', it denotes a shared-shelf relationship which must be covered by stocking at least one of the two product stands.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of market stalls along the strip — i.e., the number of distinct stall locations that could be staffed (the graph's vertices).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of neighboring (touching) stall pairs — each represents an adjacency that must have at least one volunteer at one of the two stalls (the graph's edges).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the first stall in a specific touching pair; combined with 'stall_b' it specifies one neighboring pair that must be covered by a volunteer.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the second stall in the same touching pair; together with 'stall_a' it denotes the two stalls that touch and require at least one volunteer between them.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct rooms in the house (each room is a vertex). Use this to understand how many room vertices exist when choosing the smallest set of family members to cover appliances.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of shared appliances located between pairs of rooms (each appliance is an edge). Every one of these must be adjacent to at least one room assigned to a family member.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint room identifier for a shared appliance — i.e., the first room that shares this appliance. Assigning a family member to this room covers the appliance.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint room identifier for the same shared appliance — i.e., the second room that shares this appliance. Assigning a family member to this room also covers the appliance.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of substations in the power grid (the count of vertices). This tells how many distinct substation identifiers exist in the network.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of transmission lines in the grid (the count of undirected edges). Each line connects two substations and must touch at least one upgraded site.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint substation identifier for a specific transmission line. Together with 'v' this denotes which two substations are connected by that line.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint substation identifier for the same transmission line. The pair (u, v) indicates the two substations the line links; upgrading either covers this line.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of planting beds in the patch (the number of vertices). Use this to know how many distinct bed identifiers exist when choosing which beds to water by hand.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacent bed pairs (the number of edges). Each listed adjacent pair must have at least one of its two beds selected for hand-watering.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the first bed in a specific adjacent pair. For this adjacency, either this bed or the paired bed must be hand-watered.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the second bed in the adjacent pair. For this adjacency, either this bed or the paired bed must be hand-watered.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of exhibits in the museum layout (the number of vertices). This tells you how many possible locations there are for placing guards and how exhibits are indexed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of passageways (undirected corridors) between exhibits that must be monitored. Every one of these passageways must have at least one of its endpoint exhibits guarded.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID or label) of one exhibit at one end of a specific passageway. Paired with 'v' to define a corridor; order is irrelevant because passageways are undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID or label) of the other exhibit at the opposite end of the passageway defined with 'u'. Together they specify a corridor that must have at least one guarded endpoint.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of apartments (units) in the building — i.e., the number of vertices in the graph and the complete set of flats you may choose to visit for inspections.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of shared walls between pairs of apartments — i.e., the number of edges in the graph. Each shared wall must be covered by inspecting at least one of its two adjoining apartments.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier (index or label) for one apartment that participates in a shared wall. This is one endpoint of a shared-wall pair; inspecting this apartment covers that wall.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: An identifier (index or label) for the other apartment that shares the same wall with apartment_a. This is the other endpoint of the shared-wall pair; inspecting this apartment also covers that wall.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tasks in the project (the number of distinct task vertices among which you will choose which to personally monitor).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of pairwise dependencies between tasks (each dependency is an unordered connection that must be touched by at least one task you personally monitor).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a dependency: the identifier of the first task involved in this dependency pair (one of the two tasks that must have at least one supervised endpoint).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same dependency: the identifier of the second task in this dependency pair (together with dependency_task_a it defines a dependency that your oversight roster must cover).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of servers in the infrastructure — i.e., the number of distinct machines among which you may choose some to enable enhanced logging.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct data-exchange links between servers; each such link must have at least one of its endpoint servers configured with enhanced logging.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of one endpoint server in a directly communicating pair; part of a single direct data-exchange link that needs to be covered by enabling logging on at least one endpoint.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (name or index) of the other endpoint server in the same direct data-exchange pair; together with 'server_a' this defines one link that must be covered by selecting at least one of the two servers for enhanced logging.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rooms in the house (the number of vertices). Room identifiers used elsewhere refer to these rooms.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of doorways between rooms (the number of edges). Each doorway must have at least one of its two endpoint rooms fitted with a pet gate.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one room at one end of a specific doorway. This label matches one of the room identifiers (1..total_rooms) and is used to ensure that for this doorway at least one endpoint room is gated.

item_fields.name: v

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of side-by-side adjacencies between cases; each adjacency is an edge that must have at least one of its two cases fitted with a sensor.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the first display case in a specific side-by-side pair; it is one endpoint of an adjacency that must be covered by a sensor on at least one endpoint.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (label or index) of the second display case in the same side-by-side pair; together with ‘case_one_id’ it specifies an adjacency that requires at least one fitted sensor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the lab group (the number of vertices). Use this to know how many individual students are available to assign as equipment monitors.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct student pairs who share equipment (the number of edges). Each such pair requires that at least one of the two students is assigned on duty.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one student in a pair who share gear (one endpoint of an undirected edge). Refers to a specific student label used to indicate that this student is part of a sharing relationship.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other student in the sharing pair (the other endpoint of the undirected edge). The order between student_a and student_b does not matter; together they represent a pair that needs at least one monitor.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint location identifier of the same direct route. For each (u, v) pair, at least u or v (or both) must be selected as an official drop point.

global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct submissions (papers) under consideration — each is a candidate to be assigned a reviewer. This is the number of vertices in the mutual-citation graph.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of unordered pairs of submissions that cite each other (mutual citations). Each such pair is an edge that must be covered by assigning a reviewer to at least one of its two papers.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (e.g., integer index) of one submission in a mutually-citing pair. Together with 'submission_id_b' this defines a mutual-citation edge that requires at least one of the two submissions to receive a reviewer.

item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (e.g., integer index) of the other submission in the mutually-citing pair referenced by this edge. The pair (submission_id_a, submission_id_b) denotes an undirected mutual-citation that must be covered by assigning a reviewer to at least one endpoint.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct trails in the park diagram. Each trail corresponds to a vertex you may place a single informational sign on; the optimal plan uses the fewest of these signs.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other trail meeting at the same intersection. For each listed pair (trail_id_u, trail_id_v) at least one of these trails must receive a sign so the intersection is not left confusing.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cabinet pairs that open into the same space; each pair is a requirement (edge) that at least one of the two cabinets must have a latch.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other cabinet in the same pair that share a space — the other endpoint of the pair. At least one of cabinet_endpoint_a or cabinet_endpoint_b must be latched to protect this pair.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct connections (edges) between machines. Each listed connection must have at least one of its endpoint machines with a firewall enabled.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint machine of the direct connection. Together with 'endpoint_machine_u' it defines an undirected connection that requires at least one endpoint to have a firewall enabled.

global_fields.name: num_nodes

item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other walkway in the neighboring pair. Paired with 'walkway_a', it marks an adjacency that requires at least one of the two walkways to have an emergency phone.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of floor displays in the store (the vertices). Displays are the potential positions to staff and are assumed to be labeled with identifiers referenced elsewhere (for example 1..total_displays).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct pairs of displays that physically touch each other. Each touching pair represents a constraint that at least one of the two displays must have an attendant.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one display in a touching pair (one endpoint of the edge). This refers to a labeled display between 1 and total_displays.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other display in the touching pair (the other endpoint). The pair {display_id_u, display_id_v} denotes two displays that touch; order does not matter and at least one of them must be staffed.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of separate wall pieces or sections in the room; this is the count of all pieces you may choose to treat.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of seams (joints) where two wall sections meet; each seam must be covered by treating at least one of its adjacent sections.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for one wall section that participates in a particular seam; paired with 'section_two' to describe that seam.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the other wall section at the same seam; together with 'section_one' it denotes the two sections joined by that seam.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct platform zones on the subway line; this is the number of areas you can choose to station staff in.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of end-to-end connections between zones (adjacent pairs). Each such connection must have at least one of its two zones staffed.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one platform zone that is one endpoint of an adjacent pair (one side of a connection that must be covered).

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other platform zone at the other endpoint of the adjacent pair (the other side of the connection that must be covered).

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of scaffold posts (vertices). This is the count of distinct posts available to anchor; your goal is to anchor as few of these posts as possible while ensuring every brace is covered.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of braces (edges) connecting pairs of posts. Each brace must have at least one of its endpoint posts anchored for the scaffold to be secure.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint post of a specific brace. Interpreted as the first post ID for that brace; if post_u is anchored the brace is considered secured.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint post of the brace. Interpreted as the second post ID for that brace; at least one of post_v or post_u must be anchored to cover this brace.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of junctions (intersection points) in the property where a light fixture could be installed. Each junction is a vertex in the layout and is referenced by an identifier used elsewhere.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of short corridor segments connecting pairs of junctions. Each corridor segment is an edge that must have at least one of its two adjoining junctions fitted with a light.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of one end (junction) of a specific corridor segment. Placing a light at this junction would cover this end of the corridor.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier of the other end (junction) of the same corridor segment. A light at this junction would cover the corridor from the opposite end.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of camera mounts / display-case positions in the gallery (i.e., the number of vertices). This tells you how many distinct mounts are available to place cameras on.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of direct connections between display cases that must be observed (i.e., the number of edges). Each connection is a link that requires at least one neighboring mount to have a camera.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint mount identifier (e.g., an integer label) for a specific connection between two display cases. A camera placed at this mount would observe the connection.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint mount identifier for the same connection. Either this mount or the mount_u must have a camera to cover the link between the two cases.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct students (vertices) in the school. All student IDs referenced in the interactions range over these students.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of recorded pairwise student interactions (edges). Each interaction must be overseen by assigning at least one of its two students to the monitored list.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID or index) of one student participating in this particular interaction. Together with 'student_b' it forms an unordered pair; supervising either student covers this interaction.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (ID or index) of the other student in this interaction. Along with 'student_a' it identifies the pairing that must be covered by supervising at least one participant.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of servers in the campus network (the vertex count). This tells you how many distinct servers exist to choose from when planning updates; when tallying your plan count each updated server only once.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of cable links between servers (the edge count). Each cable must touch at least one updated server for the plan to succeed.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one server at one end of a specific cable. Paired with 'v' to describe a single undirected cable; updating either endpoint covers this cable.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other server at the other end of the cable. Together with 'u' it defines the cable that must have at least one endpoint updated.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of street corners/intersections on the city map — the count of distinct places where a lamp post could be placed. Use this to know how many node identifiers exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of street segments (blocks) that run between intersections — the count of edges that must each touch at least one lit corner.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint corner (intersection) identifier for a specific street segment. If a lamp post is placed at this corner, it lights the listed segment. Matches one of the node identifiers from total_intersections.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint corner (intersection) identifier for the same street segment. The segment is considered illuminated if either corner_u or corner_v (or both) has a lamp post.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of rooms in the house (the number of vertices). Each room is a location where you can choose to install a smart sensor; this tells you how many distinct room identifiers exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of doorways between rooms (the number of edges). Every doorway must be covered by at least one sensor installed in one of the two rooms it connects.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One room adjacent to a specific doorway (one endpoint of an edge). Given this room identifier, placing a sensor here would cover that doorway. Endpoints are unordered since doorways are undirected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other room adjacent to the same doorway (the other endpoint of the edge). Installing a sensor in this room also covers the doorway; at least one of the two endpoints must have a sensor.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of workstations on the floor map; this is the number of distinct stations among which you may assign crew members.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total count of touching (adjacent) pairs of workstations; each such pair must have at least one crew member assigned to one of the two stations to be considered covered.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one workstation in an adjacent pair (one endpoint of an adjacency); used together with 'v' to denote a specific pair of touching stations that must be covered by at least one assigned staffer.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other workstation in the adjacent pair (the second endpoint); paired with 'u' to specify a particular touching pair of stations that needs coverage.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of distinct aisle positions where an usher could be posted. Each aisle position corresponds to a vertex in the graph and is identified by an integer (e.g., 1..num_aisles).

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of seat-row junctions that must be covered. Each junction is an edge in the graph and represents a place between rows that is bordered by two aisles.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One of the two aisle identifiers that border a particular seat-row junction. This is one endpoint of the edge and should match an aisle id in 1..num_aisles.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other aisle identifier that borders the same seat-row junction. This is the other endpoint of the edge and should match an aisle id in 1..num_aisles.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of tables on the restaurant floor plan — i.e., the count of table locations where you could station a floor host.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of adjacency links between tables that must be covered; each represents a pair of tables that are adjacent and therefore requires at least one of the two tables to have a host.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a specific adjacency: the identifier (table number or label) of the first table in this adjacent pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the same adjacency: the identifier (table number or label) of the second table in this adjacent pair. Assigning a host to either adjacent_table_1 or adjacent_table_2 covers this adjacency.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct set pieces on stage; the number of positions where a stagehand could be placed.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of touching relationships between set pieces; each adjacency is a pair of pieces that must be covered by at least one stagehand.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for one of the two set pieces in a touching relationship (one endpoint of an adjacency); placing a stagehand here covers this adjacency.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier for the other set piece in the touching pair (the other endpoint of an adjacency); at least one of piece_endpoint_a or piece_endpoint_b must have a stagehand to cover this adjacency.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of patients in the clinic (each graph vertex corresponds to one patient). Use this to know how many distinct patients are available to assign nurses to.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of patient pairings that must be covered (each graph edge is a pair of patients such that at least one of them must have a nurse assigned).

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of one patient in a specific pairing. For each listed pairing (u, v), this is one endpoint whose assignment status (has a nurse or not) matters for covering that pair.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier (index or label) of the other patient in a specific pairing. For each listed pairing (u, v), this is the second endpoint; at least one of patient_u_id or patient_v_id must have a nurse assigned to cover the pairing.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of apartment doors (vertices) in the floor plan under consideration. Each represents a door you could choose to fit with a lock; this count tells you how many apartment vertices exist.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of shared hallway connections (edges) between apartments. Each edge represents a corridor adjacency that must be covered by at least one locked adjoining apartment door.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of one apartment door at one end of a specific shared hallway. Together with 'v', this specifies a hallway that must have at least one of the two doors fitted with a lock.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (index or label) of the other apartment door at the opposite end of the same shared hallway. Together with 'u', this defines the hallway connection requiring at least one locked adjoining door.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of hubs in the logistics network (the vertices). These are the possible locations where fixed inspection checkpoints can be placed; hub identifiers run from 1 to this number.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of route segments between hubs (the edges). Each of these routes must be inspected by placing a checkpoint at one of its two endpoint hubs.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint hub identifier for this route segment. Together with 'v' it names the two hubs linked by the route; placing a checkpoint at either endpoint hub ensures this route is inspected.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint hub identifier for this route segment. Along with 'u' it specifies the route that must be covered by at least one inspection checkpoint at one of the two hubs.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of students in the class (the number of vertices in the friendship graph). This tells how many potential mentor candidates exist and how student identifiers range.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of friendship links among students (the number of undirected edges). Every one of these friendships must be touched by at least one selected mentor.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: One endpoint of a friendship link: the identifier (index or label) of the first student involved in this friendship edge. At least one of student_u or student_v must be chosen as a mentor to cover this friendship.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The other endpoint of the friendship link: the identifier (index or label) of the second student in this friendship edge. At least one of student_u or student_v must be chosen as a mentor to cover this friendship.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of displays in the museum layout (total vertices). Each display is a potential location for mounting an information panel; identifiers for displays run from 1 to this number.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of adjacent exhibit pairs (total edges). Each adjacency is a pair of displays that share a border or proximity and therefore must have at least one of the two displays fitted with a panel to be covered.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one display in an adjacency pair (one endpoint of an edge). This integer labels a specific display location and, together with 'display_b', defines an adjacency that must be covered by placing a panel at display_a or display_b.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other display in an adjacency pair (the other endpoint of an edge). This integer labels the second display in the adjacency; at least one of display_a or display_b must receive a panel to cover this adjacency.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of properties (houses) in the neighborhood plan. This is the number of vertices from which the organizer may choose liaisons; judges will count how many of these properties are assigned liaisons.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: The total number of bordering property pairs (adjacent property boundaries) in the map. Each bordering pair is an edge that must be covered by assigning at least one liaison to one of its two endpoint properties.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of one house in a specific bordering pair. Paired with 'property_b', this entry denotes a border between two houses; the organizer must ensure at least one of the two has a liaison.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier (label or index) of the other house in the bordering pair. Together with 'property_a' it represents a single border (edge) that needs coverage by a liaison on at least one side.

global_fields.name: num_nodes
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of distinct venue locations (vertices) in the plan — the count of places where a first aid station could be placed. Each venue is identified by an integer vertex label.

global_fields.name: num_edges
global_fields.scenario_description: Total number of direct connections between venues (edges) that must be covered. Each connection requires at least one of its endpoint venues to have a staffed first aid station.

item_fields.name: u
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of one endpoint venue for this specific connection. Together with 'v' this specifies a venue-to-venue link that must be covered by staffing at one or both endpoints.

item_fields.name: v
item_fields.scenario_description: Identifier of the other endpoint venue for this specific connection. Along with 'u', it defines a single connection that must have at least one endpoint staffed.
